parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
saw is the past tense of see, meaning observed

explanation.surface: Someone watched a power tool being used by a group of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A band-saw is a workshop machine with an endless toothed steel loop for cutting.

parts.note: a bolted door is locked

explanation.surface: A nobleman fled and was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolted' suggests running off, but here means fastened with a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blocked path is obstructed, the same as one with a bar across it.

clue.text: Describing flower that can be blue or white

definitions.text: Describing flower that can be blue or white

parts.words: Describing flower that can be blue or white
parts.note: a flower is a river, and the great African river has Blue and White branches; the adjective relates to it

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a bloom that comes in blue or white.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the Nile, the river formed where the Blue and White branches meet at Khartoum.

indicators.note: an outbreak breaks the letters of the words apart and reforms them

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A duchess comes out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Ferguson married Prince Andrew and became Duchess of York.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Ferguson held the title Duchess of York.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the given letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the Romeo loses his final letter

explanation.surface: A list of words for a lover of women: wolf, swain, Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is slang for a man who pursues women relentlessly, a philanderer.

clue.text: One who performs rubbish on the jetty

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it, so rubbish follows the jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty jutting out to sea
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A seaside entertainer does a poor act on the end of the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a clown-like entertainer in a white costume, once a fixture of seaside shows.

explanation.surface: A painter's sitter causes difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky question is a puzzle, and someone who sits in position for a painter also earns this name.

clue.text: See first at Brighton getting girth adjusted? It is a plant

parts.note: to eye something is to see it

indicators.note: first at picks the opening letter of Brighton
adjusted means the letters of girth are reset in a different order

explanation.surface: A rider in Brighton is told to check the saddle strap first, and spots a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns GIRTH into RIGHT; a girth is the strap that holds a horse's saddle on.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat sore eyes.

clue.text: Cases, of course, for old instrument in new air

indicators.note: in places the instrument inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters of air are made into a fresh order

parts.note: the viol is an early stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Boxes for an antique instrument are put on show in fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes RAI from the letters of 'air', and 'in' sets the instrument inside it. 'Cases, of course' means stuffed parcels served as a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are little pasta parcels with filling, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Hardy girl takes ages to find a piece of mosaic

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
an era is an age, a long period of time

explanation.surface: A determined girl spends ages looking for a missing piece of mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like a description of a tough girl but refers to the novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles set into a mosaic.

clue.text: Our mild characters out — beaten by the West Indians

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Some mild-mannered people of ours were outplayed by the West Indies cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten by the West Indians' reads as a cricket defeat, but it defines the drum: steel pans of the Caribbean were first made from oil drums and are played by beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribbean steel bands hammer and play instruments made from discarded steel barrels for petroleum.

explanation.surface: Someone sets things aside on ledges.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, and shelves are also flat ledges fixed to a wall.

explanation.surface: A nobleman down on his luck takes a job washing bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was the earl on the First World War recruiting poster saying 'Your country needs you', hence 'Needy'; a kitchener is also a kitchen hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl's famous poster demanded recruits, and the word also names a servant who does menial kitchen work.

parts.note: RH is the standard abbreviation for right-handed
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A gardener picks a bloom for a right-handed friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows; the Rhone runs through Switzerland and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and the Rhone is a major European river.

clue.text: Run down last month? Hard lines!

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated DEC
railway lines are hard steel tracks, and RY abbreviates railway

explanation.surface: Someone moans about being run-down last month, and a friend replies 'Hard lines!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' looks like the British exclamation meaning 'bad luck', but here it means the steel lines of a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something down is to disparage it, the same as to denounce or criticise it publicly.

parts.note: off-peak usually means a cheap phone tariff, but here the calls are sung out from the mountains, away from the peaks

explanation.surface: Someone phones at the cheaper time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers warble with rapid shifts between chest voice and falsetto, their cries carrying across valleys.

clue.text: Girl has an appalling outcome leaving this earthly paradise

indicators.note: an appalling outcome is a mess, so the letters of these words end up jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl suffers a dreadful result and is forced out of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the hidden Himalayan utopia of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, a byword for an idyll.

parts.note: airy means light, as in an airy room
a fairy is a magical being that casts spells

explanation.surface: A whimsical, delicate, magical creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes ideas that are vague and impractical.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: without tells us the letter given by 'a' is removed from the washer

parts.note: a launderer is someone who washes clothes

explanation.surface: A silent laundry worker is unmasked as a stripper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripper' suggests a striptease artist but means someone who strips a place of its goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A looter strips a town or house bare of valuables.

clue.text: Preserved in brine that is drunk

explanation.surface: Someone soaked in brine is well and truly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Onions kept in salt water or vinegar are cured this way, and a heavily intoxicated person is said to be in the same state.

clue.text: Implement that is universally silent, in a way

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, universal

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of silent are put a different way

explanation.surface: A tool which is completely silent, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially in a kitchen.

clue.text: Fine person who has a sort of square bottom

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler, so T is a sort of square
the rump is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: A decent fellow happens to have a rather square backside.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a trump is a reliable, generous fellow, a good sort.

explanation.surface: A routine custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even and unvarying is consistent, and a habit is the costume a nun or monk wears, like any official dress.

parts.note: fare means food, so the clue describes putting food into its containers before it is sold, not saving a travel fare

explanation.surface: Have your bus fare ready before boarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops sell sandwiches and meat wrapped up beforehand at a factory.

clue.text: Dance about in front of a basket

indicators.note: in front of says the letter for about goes before the dance

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: People dance round in front of a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket carried by anglers to hold their catch.

explanation.surface: Someone launches a revolting assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent is objectionable, and a military push forward is also called by this word.

indicators.note: without a starter means the opening letter of the purchased word is dropped

parts.note: bought means purchased

explanation.surface: Nothing was bought without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Ought is an old variant of nought, a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is a dated form of nought, meaning zero.

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone draws close from within hearing distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come close, to draw near.

parts.note: in cricket the number eleven batter is the last man in

indicators.note: opening picks the starting letter of the word game

explanation.surface: A tailender is promoted to open the innings for good.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the No 11 batsman is the last man in to bat, giving LAST IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring goes on for a long time, which is what permanent means.

clue.text: Girl using A1 roads, when repaired

indicators.note: when repaired means the letters are fixed into a new arrangement

parts.note: A and the numeral one, read as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman drives on Britain's A1 road once its potholes have been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, from London to Edinburgh; the 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora is a female first name, as in the dancer Isadora Duncan.

clue.text: Joy is what stopped the Camptown cricket match

definitions.text: what stopped the Camptown cricket match

explanation.surface: Happiness is what brought a cricket game in a minstrel-song town to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket stops for bad light; the song 'Camptown Races' is sung in dialect ('De Camptown ladies'), so 'the light' becomes 'de light'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy is great pleasure, and in the dialect of the song the halt to cricket is caused by 'de light', meaning poor light.

clue.text: Top dressing for some eastern dishes?

definitions.text: Top dressing for some eastern dishes?

parts.words: Top dressing for some eastern dishes?
parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive woman, so the top dressing is a veil worn over the face by some Muslim women

explanation.surface: A garnish or sauce poured over Oriental food.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the veil some Muslim women wear in public, covering the face below the eyes.
